newsitem.title: ITALY: Ciampi says Italy rate cut a step to convergence.
newsitem.headline: Ciampi says Italy rate cut a step to convergence.

text.p: Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said the Bank of Italy's decision to cut the discount rate to 7.50 percent from 8.25 confirmed that Italy was improving its finances and moving into line with other European countries.
"It confirms a positive chain of events leading to convergence with other European economies," Ciampi said in a statement.
"It is the effect of a culture of stability that is taking root in the dealings of Italians," he said.

"Interest rates have been pushed down by the drop in inflation, the recovery of credibility determined by work linked to a several budgetary policy, a policy of effective revenue and a policy of a stable exchange rate."

The 1997 budget, which parliament must approve by the end of the year, proposes to cut the public sector deficit by 62.5 trillion lire. The package is heavily weighted towards increased tax ravenues with less emphasis on spending cuts.
